metadata.title: Making Education Count for Development: Data Collection and Availability in Six PISA for Development Countries

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This report is not an analysis of student microdata from PISA-D; it documents system-level data collection and availability for the PISA-D system-level questionnaire across six participating countries. Because no student assessment scores or plausible values are analyzed, there is no application of PISA sampling weights or replicate-weight procedures in the reported work. The system-level questionnaire is described as a set of worksheets collecting contextual metadata (e.g., education system structure, national assessments/examinations, instruction time, teacher training and salaries, education finance, national accounts, and population data). For PISA-D implementation and subsequent analyses, the report’s guidance implies that analysts should ensure the completeness and comparability of these system-level inputs (and avoid duplicating data already collected by international organizations), rather than focusing on PV/weight estimation procedures.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values are not applicable because this publication does not estimate or model cognitive achievement outcomes from PISA-D student responses; it assesses the status of system-level data collection and availability for the PISA-D system-level questionnaire. Missing-data handling is not reported because there is no statistical modeling of student-level variables with missingness; instead, the report synthesizes evidence from site visits and reviews of national data systems and metadata completeness.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The report does not define an analytic student sample. It assesses system-level data collection and availability for the PISA-D system-level questionnaire in six participating countries (Cambodia, Ecuador, Guatemala, Paraguay, Senegal, Zambia) using evidence gathered during site visits (March–May 2015) and desk research (notably for Cambodia).

data.outcome_summary: This OECD report evaluates the current state of system-level data collection and availability (quality and completeness) for the PISA-D system-level questionnaire in six participating countries: Cambodia, Ecuador, Guatemala, Paraguay, Senegal, and Zambia. The system-level questionnaire is organized into ten worksheets covering education system structure, national assessments/examinations, instruction time, teacher training and salaries, educational finance (including enrolment), and national accounts/population data. Evidence is drawn from site visits conducted between March and May 2015, mainly meetings with National Project Managers and officials responsible for the relevant data domains, plus desk research for Cambodia. The report’s key results are qualitative/administrative: countries are generally able to provide the requested data, but challenges are uneven across themes—especially private education expenditure, sector coordination across ministries, and discrepancies between policy and implementation. The report provides technically sound options to improve international comparability and reduce respondent burden, rather than reporting student-level achievement metrics or ML model performance.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a system-level data documentation and readiness assessment for PISA-D, not an empirical predictive/causal study using student microdata. As a result, there is no student analytic sample size, no plausible-values-based outcome, no missing-data imputation strategy for modeled variables, and no ML algorithms or performance metrics to extract. The main contribution is descriptive guidance on data availability, metadata completeness, and cross-cutting implementation challenges for PISA-D participating countries.
